LESSON: WOOD

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Materials for Production
Topic 3.1: Wood
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Wood, part of Materials for Production in Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is wood important in day-to– day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. classify wood according to physical characteristics,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Wood in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe the preparation of wood for use in the production of items,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Wood in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. relate types of wood to their uses in the community,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Wood in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. value the importance of wood in day-to-day life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Wood in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. classify wood according to physical characteristics,

   Wood helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. describe the preparation of wood for use in the production of items,

   Wood helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. relate types of wood to their uses in the community,

   Wood helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. value the importance of wood in day-to-day life.

   Wood helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use print or digital media to search for information on types of wood,

2. discuss the physical characteristics of wood (soft and hard wood),

3. use a checklist to sort wood as either softwood or hardwood,

4. discuss methods of wood preparation (conversion and seasoning),

5. brainstorm on the uses of wood in different trades,

6. develop charts to match types of wood to their uses,

7. visit the locality to explore the uses of wood.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use print or digital media to search for information on types of wood,
2. discuss the physical characteristics of wood (soft and hard wood),
3. use a checklist to sort wood as either softwood or hardwood,
4. discuss methods of wood preparation (conversion and seasoning),
5. brainstorm on the uses of wood in different trades,
6. develop charts to match types of wood to their uses,
7. visit the locality to explore the uses of wood.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Wood together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: learner develops interacting with technology skills when using digital devices to search for information

on types of wood.

• Learning to Learn: learner acquires planning and time management skills when developing charts to match types of wood

to their uses.

Values:
• Unity: learner cooperates with others when using print or digital media to search for information on types of wood.

• Respect: learner accepts diverse opinions when discussing the methods of wood preparation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer Education and Mentorship: interpersonal relationships are enhanced as learner discusses the methods of wood

preparation.

Link to other Subjects:

Social Studies: learner enhances knowledge of resource exploitation as they brainstorm on the uses of wood in different

trades.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. classify wood according to physical characteristics,
2. describe the preparation of wood for use in the production of items,
3. relate types of wood to their uses in the community,
4. value the importance of wood in day-to-day life.

Remember the key question: Why is wood important in day-to– day life?
